provenance.note: Written by hand to illustrate schema 0.1; not evidence. What it states held at the commit that added it: tests/reference/program-ir.lean proves clamp_correct and make test-program-differential passed 686 cases.

program.stackEffect: ( value lower upper -- result true | false )

contract.statement: For integers v, l, u: if l ≤ u the word returns min(max(v, l), u) and true; if l > u it consumes its three inputs and returns false. Cells below are kept.

check.label: checked by the Lean reference, not by LeanForth
check.note: The theorems are about the IR's semantics, not about Gforth running the source.

verify.note: Verification conditions are generated from 2.5.5 on.

assumptions.text: Every value is one signed host cell; the Lean theorems hold for every cell width of at least two bits, the runtime tests ran on 64-bit cells.
Cells use two's complement, so arithmetic wraps as the IR semantics says; the clamp itself does no arithmetic.
The reader translated the colon definition into the IR faithfully; nothing checks the translation itself.
Gforth and its compiler execute 2DUP, >, IF, 2DROP, DROP, >R, MAX, R>, MIN, TRUE, FALSE and EXIT as the IR semantics says.
The data and return stacks have room for the word's items; underflow and overflow are not proved absent on the host.
Lean 4.35.0 (the pinned toolchain) checked the theorems correctly.
